questions.q: What real problem does a Terraform module solve, according to this lesson?
options: Modules are required before a provider can be declared
Modules eliminate the need for a state file
Terraform cannot run `apply` at all without at least one module defined
The maintenance trap of a resource block copy-pasted across multiple environments or teams, where a fix has to be manually repeated in every copy
questions.explain: Copy-pasting the same resource block into dev, staging, and prod means every fix — like adding an NSG — has to land in every copy by hand, and it's easy to miss one.

questions.q: What is a Terraform module, structurally?
options: A built-in Terraform command with no associated files
A feature that only exists inside Terraform Cloud, never locally
A folder of .tf files with its own input variables and outputs, callable from a module block
A special file extension (.tfmod) that only HashiCorp can author
questions.explain: A module is not an exotic engine feature — it's just a directory of ordinary .tf files that accepts inputs and produces outputs, called with a module block.

questions.q: According to the lesson's rule of thumb, when should you actually extract a module?
options: Only after the configuration has been deployed to production for at least a year
Once the same resource block has been copy-pasted two or three times, especially across environments or teams
Before writing any resource blocks at all, to stay 'DRY' from the start
Never — Terraform configurations should always use flat resource blocks
questions.explain: Writing a module too early adds indirection that isn't worth paying for until there's real duplication to remove; the practical threshold is two to three repetitions.

questions.q: What is the root module in a Terraform configuration?
options: The very first module ever published to the Terraform Registry
The module with the highest version number in a configuration
The working directory that terraform init, plan, and apply run from, which can call other modules but isn't one itself
A module that must be named 'root' in its source argument
questions.explain: The root module is simply the directory where you run the Terraform CLI; it can call child modules via module blocks, but it isn't itself called by anything.

questions.q: The lesson draws a parallel between a Terraform module and which concept from earlier in this learning path?
options: A PowerShell function that wraps a copy-pasted loop so the logic exists in one place with one name
An Excel pivot table that summarizes raw data
A Git branch used for feature development
A SQL stored procedure that returns a result set
questions.explain: Just like wrapping a copy-pasted PowerShell loop in a function gives that logic one name and one home, a module does the same for a repeated block of HCL.
